title: Not exactly a game, but I built an interactive musical instrument that I have been playing like one.
author: Acetotheface85
selftext:
I know this isn't a traditional game, but I've honestly been playing with it like one, and I thought this community might appreciate the development side of it.

I've been building something called **FIFTHWAVE**, a browser-based harmonic instrument that explores a different way of interacting with music.

The latest evolution is **Cosmic Duet**, which takes the original concept and turns it into a two-handed, multi-touch experience built around two independent harmonic circles.

Turn your phone sideways, put a finger on each circle, and start exploring. You can glide between notes and chords, layer harmonies, and create music through movement rather than traditional keys.

Each circle has its own key, octave, and instrument controls. I've also added sustain, looping, recording, playback, and audio export.

What's been interesting to me is how much this has started to feel like a game. There's something surprisingly engaging about discovering harmonies, experimenting with combinations, and figuring out how the two circles interact. You don't necessarily need to understand music theory to start having fun with it.

I've also been exploring how AI can help me develop and iterate on ideas like this, particularly when experimenting with unconventional interfaces and interactions.

**No installation, no account. Just open it in your browser and play.**

Headphones recommended.

I would love to hear what this community thinks, especially about the interaction design and whether something like this could evolve even more.

**Try it:** [https://studio.fifthwave.towellcreative.com/cosmic-duet](https://studio.fifthwave.towellcreative.com/cosmic-duet)
